records.name: Valdonis
records.facts_used: Valdonis: Siliņš connects the name with Latvian valdonis, ruler or master. A common noun has become a personal name. This local lexical link is explicit; the origins of similar Vald- names must be checked individually. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Valdonis: 1886, Riga. Its calendar year is 1880. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p315 exact valdonis lexical explanation and own Riga 1886/calendar 1880; no other Vald-form dates transferred.

records.name: Aistis
records.facts_used: Aistis: The name was formed from the Baltic ethnonym aisčiai. A people’s designation became a personal name; the ethnonym’s further etymology is a separate question. This formation does not yield one secure literal translation of its ancient root. Aistis is known as poet Jonas Aleksandravičius’s chosen literary name. The encyclopaedia dates Be tėvynės brangios to 1942. Here it illustrates a literary name, rather than a given name recorded at birth.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Guide explicit ethnonym formation; VLE exact literary name and 1942collection. Salys surname-only listing is not accepted as a given-name first attestation.

records.name: Dovydas
records.facts_used: Dovydas: Lithuanian Dovydas is a form of the David family, from a Hebrew name meaning beloved. Its spelling and pronunciation have changed across languages. That connection explains the family without dating the first Lithuanian child bearing it. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Dovydas (Dovas) on 11 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Visually checked Salys PDF p. 318/printed p. 303 December11 exact Dovydas(Dovas); DMNES confirms Hebrew beloved.

records.name: Tautvaldė
records.facts_used: Tautvaldė: The Lithuanian compound combines taut-, connected with tauta, people, and vald-, connected with valdyti, to rule. The feminine form corresponds to Tautvaldas. Explaining the stems does not force them into one literal sentence. Page 93 of the 2011 study gives Tautvaldė alongside Tautvaldas. This is dated evidence for the exact form in scholarly work. Publication does not mark a first birth record or the name’s invention.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Pakerys 2011 PDF p. 4/printed p. 93 visually checked feminine Taũtvaldė(plg.Taũtvaldas); masculine Salys calendar record not substituted for exact feminine form.

records.name: Taaniel
records.facts_used: Taaniel: The family continues Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge. Taaniel is an Estonian full form, while Tani is documented as a short name in that family. Shortening changes the form while retaining its connection to the historical base. Page 47 of Mägiste’s 1929 name list gives Taaniel as the full form linked to Tanel and Tanil. This is specific dated evidence for the local form. The dictionary’s publication year is not the name’s invention date or a first birth record.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Mägiste PDF p. 49/printed p. 47 explicit Tanel=Taaniel and Tanil=Taaniel. Question mark by Tani not erased; no 1929invention claim.

records.name: Tani
records.facts_used: Tani: The family continues Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge. Taaniel is an Estonian full form, while Tani is documented as a short name in that family.
